implemented_boundary: Verified non-operating close-policy admission, PrepareClose and CloseWithoutRestart through the authoritative application, writer and development HTTP. Closed case is independent from native outcome, resource release and restart.
verified_properties: Current lead and scope access before cached replies; exact body/key and cell/case cohort CAS.
Bound policy, context, generation, evidence, time and personnel/handover; changed basis cannot consume clearance.
Prepare/consume rollback and committed response loss preserve one clearance/closure result.
Atomic clearance consumption, case membership/closure and distinct OUT_OF_SERVICE latch; other case blocks retained.
UNKNOWN outcome and resource holder/quarantine preserved; no Arm generated.
New physical report invalidates personnel/handover; duplicate immutable reports never replay old workflow; closed cases preserve new facts and restrictions.
known_incomplete_boundaries: Normal successful close is application-tested; HTTP rejection paths tested. Dedicated closure UI/browser flow, ordinary operator-service session and full frozen gRPC close projection are not implemented.
No-entry diagnostic closure, uncertain scopes, changed configurations, lead transfer and multiple originating-cell cohorts remain unsupported.
Production close/procedure verifier and physical containment/personnel procedures are not qualified. Test authority and facts are simulation only.
Recovery/restart/cancel/control session, full journal retention, supervisor, mandatory own stack, two product images and install/update/restore remain incomplete.
prior_evidence_not_rerun: Existing browser UI layout and Linux/C++ planner validation remain prior scope; this turn changes only a UI block enum/label and platform intervention/closure behavior. Production planner/native code unchanged.
resolved_development_failures: Initial test helper method names corrected to existing inspect_case/put_principal APIs; no normative or production gate was relaxed.

source_archive.scope: Reported source/SDK/UI inventory. Toolchains, node_modules, image layers, runtime databases and private credentials excluded.
